current_example.title: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

q-43889.name: Question 1
q-43889.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨2,-1,6⟩,$ $⟨7,2,0⟩,$ and $⟨1,-4,6⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-43889.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -4 \\ 6 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

q-43889.html:
Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨2,−1,6⟩, ⟨7,2,0⟩, and ⟨1,−4,6⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [271−142606]
b
 [271−12−4606]
c
 [2−167201−46]
d
 [271−124606]
e
 [217−1−42660]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[271−12−4606].

q-43832.name: Question 2
q-43832.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-1⟩$ and $⟨2,3⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-43832.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−1⟩ and ⟨2,3⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [213−1]
b
 [12−13]
c
 [−1213]
d
 [13−12]
e
 [1−123]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[12−13].

q-43891.name: Question 3
q-43891.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨2,4⟩$ and $⟨1,-5⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-43891.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

q-77950.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-77950.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

q-43892.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,4⟩$ and $⟨5,-1⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-43892.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-43892.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,4⟩ and ⟨5,−1⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [1451]
b
 [−1541]
c
 [154−1]
d
 [15−41]
e
 [145−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[154−1].

q-77999.name: Question 6
q-77999.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/09423b097ab02b339f15af831e0e35f59ff88cb00c0ef72d3693ce9f24e6b9dc.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-77999.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

q-77999.html:
Question 6
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[13−2−3]
b
[1−2−33]
c
[1−23−3]
d
[−2−313]
e
[−21−33]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[−2−3] and j′=[13].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[−21−33].

q-43894.name: Question 7
q-43894.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/5aaf29ab4dd2de3d104ca37a71ee66078f985b908465a77ca06ba8ffadd50210.png)

In the diagram above,  $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and  ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-43894.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-43837.html:
Question 8
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [112−1]
b
[1−12−1]
c
[−121−1]
d
 [−1−112]
e
 [12−1−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[12] and j′=[−1−1].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[1−12−1].

q-77990.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/20aff9b0dd1ea6aaab8cfa932317e83015956ac355349d5ae3d744de289bdae5.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-77990.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-77996.name: Question 10
q-77996.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
q-77996.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-77955.name: Question 11
q-77955.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
q-77955.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

q-77955.html:
Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[30−72]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[32] and [0−7]
b
[02] and [3−7]
c
[−72] and [30]
d
[3−7] and [02]
e
[30] and [−72]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[3−7]T(j)=T[01]=[02]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[30−72][10]=[3−7]T(j)=T⋅j=[30−72][01]=[02]

q-43890.name: Question 12
q-43890.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
q-43890.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-43890.html:
Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[5−2341−58−13]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
 [548], [−2−11], and [3−53]
b
 [5−23], [41−5], and [8−13]
c
 [584], [−2−11], and [33−5]
d
 [548], [−21−1], and [3−53]
e
 [5−23], [4−15], and [813]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[548]T(j)=T[010]=[−21−1]T(k)=T[001]=[3−53]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[5−2341−58−13][100]=[548]T(j)=T⋅j=[5−2341−58−13][010]=[−21−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[5−2341−58−13][001]=[3−53]

q-43893.name: Question 13
q-43893.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
q-43893.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-43893.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[4−451]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
 [−45] and [41]
b
 [4−4] and [51]
c
 [45] and [−41]
d
 [41] and [−45]
e
 [−41] and [45]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[45]T(j)=T[01]=[−41]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[4−451][10]=[45]T(j)=T⋅j=[4−451][01]=[−41]

q-77959.name: Question 14
q-77959.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
q-77959.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-77959.html:
Question 14
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
b
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
c
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
d
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
e
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[1−30]T(j)=T[010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T[001]=[−1−20]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−4−1−35−20−10][100]=[1−30]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−4−1−35−20−10][010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−4−1−35−20−10][001]=[−1−20]

q-139994.name: Question 15
q-139994.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
q-139994.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-139994.html:
Question 15
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−2341−1110]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
 [114], [−211], and [30−1]
b
 [141], [−211], and [3−10]
c
 [141], [2−11], and [310]
d
 [123], [41−1], and [110]
e
 [1−23], [41−1], and [110]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[141]T(j)=T[010]=[−211]T(k)=T[001]=[3−10]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−2341−1110][100]=[141]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−2341−1110][010]=[−211]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−2341−1110][001]=[3−10]
